text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- "Poland should join the EU and NATO by 2000," France's President Jacques Chirac declared in Polish parliament on Thursday.
- Pepsico has invested $292 million in Poland and is the sixth biggest investor, Poland's Foreign Investments Agency (PAIZ) said.

- Poland's Business Centre Club (BCC) has presented France's President Jacques Chirac with a BCC Golden Statue. The Statute is a reward the Club grants for contributions to free market economy development in this country.
- The Szczecin-based Gryfia shipyard will construct three ferries for Swinoujscie municipal authorities until 1998.
- Polish fishing companies will buy 66 tonnes of hake from Canadian fishermen this month.

- Gdansk Refinery will decrease diesel oil sales from 120,000 tonnes to 80,000 tonnes due to unprofitable imports' cuts. In some Poland's agricultural areas petrol stations will soon run out of diesel fuel as farmers have started buying out all reserves.
- U.S. General Motors auto-maker will start construction of the Gliwice-based Opel aasembly plant in October this year.

- A Polish capital group -- including trading firm Universal, which wants to buy large press distribution chain Ruch -- will be able to pay 120 million zlotys for the controlling stake in the network and additionally invest 200 million zlotys there.
NOWA EUROPA
- CEFTA countries prime ministers meet in Slovakia on Friday to discuss tariff cuts.
- The Supreme Administrative Court has ruled that the treasury would not have to refund foreign trade company Stalexport 75 million zlotys in interest on overpaid taxes.
- Poland and France signed an agreement on police cooperation to fight drug smuggling, illegal immigration and other crimes yesterday.
- The new collective labour agreement grants Poland's steel mill workers 120 percent of the average minimum pay and a 40 hour working week.
- Electric power plant Jaworzno 3 has installed exhausts desulphuring equipment worth around 400 million zlotys, in one of Poland's biggest environmental projects currently underway.
- Germany's Ytong cement maker has started readymix concrete production in its recently modernised plant in Ostroleka, central Poland.
- Around 130 companies from Poland and abroad have exhibited arms and military equipment in the Defence Industry Fair in Kielce, southern Poland.
- Following a wave of warning strikes, Poland's physicians demonstrate in Warsaw to demand more money and health service reforms.
- The Gdynia-based Bank Komunalny SA municipal bank will enter the Warsaw bourse, the bank said in a statement.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Parliamentary committees have upheld most of last year's regulations on corporate taxation, which the finance ministry seeks to change. The tax will remain at the 40 percent level and the investment related tax brakes will be maintained.
- A serious foreign investor is interested in buying assets of the bankrupt Gdansk Shipyard, Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said. "The investor is not South Korean", he added.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- Poland's economy is at the fore of the emerging markets' countries though further development is threatened by a lack of balance between exports and investments and low domestic demand.
- Macdonalds has set up 28 drive-through restaurants in around Poland since last year, and the number is likely to grow, the firm's officials said.
PARKIET
- Over 90 exhibitors will take part in the Second Polish Capital Investments Forum in Warsaw, scheduled for October.

- The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) has approved for public trade stock of the environmental protection bank BOS and new share issues of computer maker Optimus, Petrobank, printing company Echo Press and loudspeaker maker Tonsil.
